headline: High: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate content while the prompt-engineering repo offers no isolation or runtime controls, creating default data-leak and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b has file inputs and API calls but no documented ingestion of agent_a outputs. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a text into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, reassess for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy generated text from agent_a into agent_b without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches account data and uploads media via broad network egress, but agent_a has no data classes touched and no filesystem or network surface. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace, so leakage is limited unless an operator bridges them manually.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF sensitive media or account files are copied from agent_a into agent_b inputs, those contents may leave the host via agent_b.
mitigations: Store agent_b inputs in a separate directory.
Avoid placing secrets or account files in any shared folder.
Review outbound uploads before running agent_b.
Use a throwaway account for testing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is not runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities. agent_b cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so capability conflict is effectively blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a is made runnable with write or network permissions, reassess overlap.
IF agent_b is granted filesystem write or git mutation, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as read-only reference material.
Do not grant agent_b write or git permissions.
Run each agent in separate directories.
Use a single orchestrator lock if future write access is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a prompt-engineering resource that could be treated as guidance, while agent_b performs uploads and API calls. The pair could cascade if operator or orchestration treats agent_a content as authoritative instructions for agent_b, but no default automated handoff is documented.
conditions: IF agent_a output is pasted into agent_b as operational instructions, cascading error becomes likely.
IF agent_b is configured to act on unreviewed text from agent_a, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before using agent_a outputs.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
Add a checklist for any upload action.
Log the source of any instructions fed into agent_b.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles account data and uploads media to external services, while agent_a is a general prompt repository with no stated compliance controls. The mismatch is not a direct residency violation, but the pair lacks documented retention, deletion, or certification alignment, so compliance gaps exist in default use.
conditions: IF account data or user media processed by agent_b is subject to retention limits, the gap becomes material.
IF the operator requires documented deletion or export handling, neither profile shows it.
mitigations: Confirm what account data agent_b stores.
Avoid uploading regulated content.
Keep a manual deletion log.
Review vendor terms before production use.
